title: Clean and analyse a month of sales in a spreadsheet
done_when: A workbook with the raw data on one sheet, a cleaned table, three formulas (SUMIFS, XLOOKUP or VLOOKUP, IF) and one pivot table that answers a question you wrote at the top
evidence: The workbook file or a shared link, and the one-line question and answer

title: Build a one-page dashboard from open Malaysian data
done_when: One page with at least three charts from an OpenDOSM table, each chart titled with the finding it shows, and the table's source and date on the page
evidence: A screenshot or link and the OpenDOSM table's URL

title: Answer five business questions with SQL
done_when: Five queries on a sample database (joins, GROUP BY, a subquery), each with the question in a comment and the result pasted under it
evidence: A .sql file or notebook with the queries and results

title: Automate a repetitive file task with Python
done_when: A script that renames, merges or summarises a folder of files you would otherwise do by hand, with a README saying how to run it and how long it saves
evidence: The script and README (a public repository or a zip)

title: Check an AI-written report line by line
done_when: An AI tool drafts a one-page summary of a document you know; you mark every claim as correct, wrong or unsupported and write the corrected page
evidence: The AI draft, your marked-up copy and the corrected page

title: Write a professional email and a short report
done_when: A 150-word email announcing a change to a team, and a two-page report with headings, a summary first and one table, both read aloud and edited twice
evidence: Both documents with the first and final drafts

title: Give a five-minute presentation with a Q&A
done_when: Five slides at most, delivered to at least three people, with two questions answered and their feedback written down
evidence: The slides, and the feedback notes (or a recording)

title: Reconcile a bank statement with a ledger
done_when: A month of sample transactions matched between a statement and a ledger, every difference listed with its reason and a closing balance that agrees

title: Handle three difficult customer cases in writing
done_when: Written replies to three realistic complaints (a refund, a delay, an angry repeat caller), each with what you would check first and when you would hand the case to a person above you
evidence: The three replies and your notes

title: Plan a small project with a timeline and budget
done_when: A plan for a real or realistic small project: tasks, owners, a timeline chart, a budget in RM and the three biggest risks with what you would do about each

title: Build and publish a one-page website
done_when: A page you wrote in HTML and CSS that works on a phone, describing a project of yours, published on a free host
evidence: The page's URL and its source code

title: Teach someone a skill you have
done_when: A 20-minute lesson to one or more people with a goal, a short exercise and a check that they can now do it
evidence: Your lesson plan and what the learner could do at the end

title: Interview someone in the job you want
done_when: A 30-minute conversation with a person in the target occupation, ten questions prepared, and a one-page note on what their week looks like and which tasks AI already helps with
evidence: Your questions and the one-page note (no personal details of the person)

title: Write a customer survey and summarise 20 answers
done_when: A ten-question survey, at least 20 answers, and a one-page summary with two charts and three recommendations
evidence: The survey, the anonymised answers and the summary

title: Do a safety walk-through of a workplace
done_when: A checklist-based walk-through of a workshop, kitchen or site, ten hazards recorded with the control you would put in place for each
evidence: The checklist with photos of the hazards (no people in them)

title: Troubleshoot and document a fault
done_when: A fault on a device, machine or computer found step by step, each test and its result written down, and the fix (or the reason to call a specialist)
evidence: The troubleshooting log and a before-and-after photo

title: Write a job-ready CV for one target occupation
done_when: A one- or two-page CV aimed at one occupation, every line showing a result, with the tools and skills the occupation lists in its O*NET profile that you can prove

title: Explain a data trend to a non-expert
done_when: One chart from public data and a two-minute explanation of what it shows and what it does not, given to someone outside the field, with their one-sentence summary written down
evidence: The chart, your script and their summary
